title: The Real Lesson of the Iran War
gist: Justin Bronk of RUSI says Iran's resilience against Israel and the US perplexes many, despite thousands of strikes on targets and the killing of top leaders. Only the opening is available (paywall), so his own explanation of when airpower wins is not visible.

insights.claim: Israel and the United States have hit thousands of Iranian targets, destroyed much of Iran's military infrastructure and killed many top leaders, yet the Islamic Republic has survived and kept significant offensive capabilities.
insights.speaker: Justin Bronk
insights.so_what: Airpower alone has not ended Iran's capacity to retaliate, which keeps regional energy and shipping risk elevated.

insights.claim: Some explanations for Iran's resilience point to its effective use of low-cost precise mass weapons such as the Shahed-136 one-way attack drone; others to its decentralized, self-replacing structure.
insights.speaker: Justin Bronk
insights.so_what: Cheap mass munitions versus expensive defenses is a cost-exchange problem relevant to air-defense and drone-sector demand.
